title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck is building a combinatorial, order-theoretic foundation for 'découpages' (dissections) of surfaces, from which 'réseaux' are to be obtained. The one-dimensional building block is a 'tranche' L. Page 16 defines it as an object of the largest full subcategory C of ordered sets satisfying four conditions: (a) every L in C is filtered up and down and has cardinality ≥2; (b) L is dense (x<y implies some z with x<z<y); (c) every nonempty upper section L_{>x} is again in C; (c') the dual of (c). He calls such sets 'Thomson ordonnés'. Concretely these are dense linear-order-like 'segments', abstract models of an arc or a line.

This page develops the elementary interval topology of a tranche L.

(1) Closed sub-tranches (sous-tranches fermées). These are subsets of four forms:
- [a,b] with a<b;
- L_{≤a} with a not the least element;
- L_{≥b} with b not the greatest element;
- L itself.
The non-degeneracy conditions keep each one of cardinality ≥2, so it is again a tranche for the induced structure.

(2) Boundary. For each form he sets ∂I = {a,b}, resp. {a}, resp. {b}, resp. ∅.

(3) Relative position. Two closed sub-tranches are said to be in 'ordinary' (later 'moderate') relative position under a condition on their boundaries. The condition is mostly illegible; apparently it says the boundary of one does not meet the other, or the boundaries are disjoint. Several heavily crossed-out lines concern intersections of such sub-tranches and their boundaries.

(4) Ordinary closed parts of L. These are subsets that are the union of a finite family of pairwise disjoint closed sub-tranches, pairwise in ordinary relative position.

(5) Open intervals. These are ]a,b[ for a<b, together with L_{>a} and L_{<a}. For a closed sub-tranche I, the interior I° is I minus its boundary.

In modern terms this is the description of closed 'definable' (tame) subsets of a dense linear order: finite unions of closed intervals and rays, with frontier the finite set of endpoints. The page prepares the theorem on page 18. There, for a 'well-dominated' découpage, a finite family of disjoint closed pseudo-découpages in moderate relative position is shown to be unique (it is the family of connected components of its union), and the boundary of the union is the union of the boundaries. This yields the notion of a 'moderate closed part'.
errors: No substantive error is visible in the legible parts. The definitions are consistent: excluding a = min in L_{≤a}, b = max in L_{≥b}, and requiring a<b in [a,b] ensures each closed sub-tranche has ≥2 elements, as page 16's condition (a) requires.

The crossed-out passage apparently claims that two closed sub-tranches in ordinary relative position have empty intersection. This is not true without a disjointness hypothesis. Grothendieck seems to have deleted it and moved disjointness into the definition of 'partie fermée ordinaire' (and into hypothesis a) on page 18).

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'tranche' (Thomson ordered set) with closed sub-intervals, rays and their endpoint boundaries
ideas.modern_name: Interval topology on a dense linear order; one-dimensional cells of an o-minimal structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical order topology; o-minimal formalisation by van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn (1984–86)
ideas.where_published: Only the programmatic 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this specific formalism is unpublished

ideas.what: Ordinary/moderate closed parts as finite disjoint unions of closed sub-tranches in good relative position
ideas.modern_name: Closed definable subsets of a line in an o-minimal structure (finite unions of points and intervals); cell decomposition in dimension 1

ideas.what: 'Position relative modérée' as a condition on boundaries, used to build combinatorial dissections (découpages)
ideas.modern_name: Transversality/genericity condition in combinatorial or tame stratifications
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 on tame topology and dissections

missed.claim: This is part of an unpublished, purely order-theoretic axiomatisation of tame one-dimensional topology ('tranches' = Thomson ordered sets), intended as the base layer for 'réseaux via découpages' of surfaces. That programme of tame topology founded on ordered sets rather than on structures over a field was never published. The page itself is routine, but the overall approach (a category of dense ordered sets closed under taking rays) is an independent route toward o-minimal-style foundations.
missed.quote: Partie fermée ordinaire de I : toute partie qui est [réunion] d'une famille finie de sous-tranches fermées disjointes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest for the relation between Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' and o-minimality. The content of this page alone is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: These are elementary definitions of closed intervals, endpoints, interiors and finite unions in a dense order. They are standard and coincide with dimension-1 o-minimal definable sets. They are of interest only as a fragment of the unpublished tame-topology programme.
transcription_corrections: The header 'fermée I' is likely a later insertion qualifying 'sous-tranche' ('Sous-tranche fermée d'une tranche L').
'pour la structure de ... [?]' likely reads 'pour la structure induite' (tranche structure induced from L).
'pos. rel.' is presumably 'position relative' ('en position relative ordinaire'), later called 'modérée' on page 18.
In the open-interval line, the rays should presumably read L_{>a} and L_{<b} (with conditions on a, b).
